intervals.label: proposed (design paper and pathfinder results)
intervals.locator: arXiv abstract page of the design paper (Nature Astronomy 7, 1497 (2023))
intervals.note: Start is the arXiv submission month of the design paper. The paper schedules a 10-string pilot project at the selected site for about 2026 and construction of the full array after a successful demonstration; no source seen reports that either has started, so no construction interval is entered.

placements.note: Region-grade (about 10 km) position stated to 0.1 degree in the design paper.
placements.quote: an area near 114.0◦ E, 17.4◦ N was selected as a suitable location to build a large scale deep-sea detector

instrumented_volume.quote: This arrangement will result in a world-leading instrumented geometric volume of ∼ 7.5 km3

string_count.quote: The detector contains 1211 strings, each containing 20 hDOMs separated vertically by 30 m

summary.plain: A planned seafloor array of about 24,000 light-sensing modules on 1,211 strings that detects the faint blue Cherenkov flashes produced when neutrinos interact in the sea water.
summary.technical: Proposed array of 1211 strings with 20 hybrid digital optical modules each (multi-PMT plus SiPM), vertical spacing 30 m, 2800-3400 m below sea level, Penrose-tiling string pattern with 70 m and 110 m spacings, ~7.5 km^3.

technology.quote: the TRIDENT hDOM design adds SiPMs with excellent timing resolution, placed in the spaces between PMTs
technology.value: Hybrid digital optical modules (multiple small PMTs plus SiPMs) on seafloor strings detecting Cherenkov light in sea water
